sections.html:
Roughly 35 miles north of Salt Lake City and west of the Wasatch range, West Haven is a city in Weber County. Neighbors are Ogden on the east, Roy on the south, Hooper on the west and Marriott-Slaterville on the north. Two rivers, the Weber and the Ogden, join in the northeast corner, around 4,269 feet up. Because the city belongs to the Ogden-Clearfield metro area, plenty of residents drive to jobs in Ogden, Roy and Davis County.

Population was 10,272 in 2010 and 16,739 in 2020, and the July 2025 estimate at the top of this page is 25,627. A citywide sewer system arrived in 2002 and made denser building possible. West Haven became a city on July 1, 1991, when the old communities of Kanesville and Wilson combined, so farmhouses, older grid streets and new subdivisions all share one set of city limits. That is why two houses here can sell very differently.

Homeowner vacancy was just 0.7% in 2020, so very few houses stand empty.

Winters are cold and summers hot. Ogden, close by, sees an average July high of 91.3 degrees, a January low of 21.2 and about 16.4 inches of precipitation yearly, with a record low of minus 23 and a record high of 106. Snowfall typically starts around late October or early November and runs to April.

Those swings punish certain parts of a house:

  • Roofs and gutters holding snow and ice.
  • Exposed pipes and sprinkler lines that can freeze.
  • Furnaces, which run hard half the year.
  • Driveways and flatwork that crack through freeze and thaw cycles.

Inspectors check all of these, and an aging furnace often turns into a bargaining point.

By census definition the city is entirely urban, yet it still has a farm feel. Most neighborhoods are single-family, condominiums and multifamily buildings are being added, and some 19th-century farmhouses and working farms remain. The city bought 40 acres for a park in 1994, with playground equipment, sports fields and a historical marker. A River Parkway Trail is planned with a fishing bridge and a pedestrian tunnel under 21st Street, linking to the Weber County Centennial Trail.

A house close to the trails and schools draws families. One on a bigger rural lot draws people who want space for animals or outbuildings.

The Weber School District serves the city. Elementary schools in or near it are Country View, Haven Bay, Kanesville and West Haven, and junior high students attend Rocky Mountain or the newer Mountain View. Two of these buildings opened as recently as 2024, which shows how quickly families have arrived. Buyers with children often ask which school a house feeds, so confirm the boundary with the district before you advertise.

West Haven's Community Development group handles the Building Department, business licensing, code enforcement and emergency management. The city offices are at 4150 S 3900 W, and the main line is 801-731-4519. Ask which permits apply before you begin repairs, and ask your title or escrow company what the buyer's lender will want to see.

A quick pre-listing checklist:

  • Finished basements, decks and sheds should have permits on file.
  • Open code complaints should be cleared with code enforcement.
  • Utility accounts, including the West Haven Special Service District bill, should be current.

sections.h2: Weber County property tax and recording
sections.html:
The county sends one property tax bill a year, payable by November 30. After that date the balance is delinquent on December 1 and penalties and interest are added. Expect valuation notices around July 20, tax notices in October, and an appeal deadline of September 15.

Utah takes 45% off the value of a primary residence, leaving 55% to tax. Weber County requires the home to be the occupant's main residence for at least 183 consecutive days in a year, and a renter's main home can qualify too. Nightly rentals, vacation homes and second homes cannot. When the county mails a declaration form, return it within 30 days or the exemption is dropped. The Assessor's line is (801) 399-8572 if you are unsure where you stand.

The Weber County Recorder takes deeds at 2380 Washington Blvd, Suite 370, in Ogden. The charge is $45.00 for the first page, none for further standard pages, and $2.00 per description beyond ten. At closing, the title company prorates property tax.

Sellers here have three paths: an agent listing, a sale by owner, or a cash offer. Which one fits depends on how much work the house needs and how soon you need to be done. Roof and furnace condition tend to set the price a buyer will offer.

Cash Home Buyers purchases Utah houses in their current shape. People who call us are often up against a deadline, such as a job change, an inherited property, a tenant situation, or a mortgage that has slipped behind. The process is simple: talk through the house, schedule a walk-through, receive a written offer, and pick the closing date. Bring the deed, the latest tax notice and any loan statement so the title company can confirm what is owed. Saying no costs you nothing.

On closing day the title company pays off your mortgage, divides the year's property tax between you and the buyer, and files the new deed with the Weber County Recorder. Any unpaid tax is deducted from your proceeds, since the debt follows the parcel. A balance goes delinquent on December 1, and interest accrues on the previous year's balance from February 1. Paying it off before listing keeps the closing statement simple.

Request a payoff figure from the title company early, and ask who is covering the $45.00 first-page recording charge. Cash deals often close sooner because no lender is underwriting a loan, which lets you line the date up with a move.

sections.h2: What West Haven sellers often face
sections.html:
• Competition from newly built houses in a city that has grown by tens of percent in a few years.
  • Older farmhouses and rural lots where the land and the house are valued differently.
  • Primary residence exemption questions when a house becomes a rental.
  • Out-of-state heirs who must sort out a deed and a recording before anything else.

If you inherited the house, the deed and recording come first, then the tax notice and any open balance. If you rented it out, confirm how the county currently treats the exemption before you close. Sellers who lived in the house for years sometimes forget they changed its use, and the Assessor can tell you what is on file for the parcel.

faqs.q: What county is West Haven, UT in?
faqs.a: Weber County. Property tax, deeds and valuation appeals all go through Weber County offices in Ogden.

faqs.q: When is property tax due in West Haven?
faqs.a: The due date is November 30. A balance still open on December 1 is delinquent, and interest on the prior year's balance starts February 1.

faqs.q: What does it cost to record a deed in Weber County?
faqs.a: The Recorder charges $45.00 for the first page, nothing for additional standard pages, and $2.00 for each legal description over ten.

faqs.q: Which school district covers West Haven?
faqs.a: The Weber School District. Nearby elementary schools include Country View, Haven Bay, Kanesville and West Haven, with Rocky Mountain and Mountain View junior highs.

faqs.q: Can I sell a West Haven house as-is?
faqs.a: Yes. No rule makes you repair a house first. A buyer who purchases it in present condition lets you skip the repair bills.
